thread:
Maria (Support): Customer reports embeddings chart showing 'tokens' on the Y axis but numbers line up with vectors. Billing spike ~3x yesterday. customer id bd-4471. Screenshot: https://redwood-s3.internal/bd-4471/embeds-spike.png 
Sam (Eng): Can you paste the exact console path/time range and one or two sample request ids?
Maria (Support): Path: Console > Analytics > Embeddings > 30d. Time range 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-11. Sample req ids: req_0a1b2c, req_0a1b2d. Tooltip shows "12,000 tokens" on hover. Customer says billing charged vectors *and* tokens.
Sam (Eng): Thanks. I'm going to check ingestion/rollup. @Lee can you grep rollup for bd-4471 + those req ids?
Lee (Analytics): Running quick aggregation now. SQL I ran: ```sql
SELECT unit, SUM(value) as total
FROM embeddings_rollup
WHERE customer_id='bd-4471'
  AND ts >= '2026-03-10' AND ts < '2026-03-12'
GROUP BY unit;
```
Lee (Analytics): Result snippet: vectors: 12000, tokens: 12000 — both present for same buckets.
Sam (Eng): That matches the customer's observation. UI currently sums whatever units exist for the selected timeframe and then picks a label based on first-seen unit. If both 'vectors' and 'tokens' are present we end up double-counting and mislabeling. Bug. :thinking_face: 
Maria (Support): Customer is pushing for refund if billing is wrong. They want ETA.
Lee (Analytics): Hypothesis: during the ingest pipeline migration a new event emitter started emitting `vector_count` while legacy pipeline still emitted `token_count` for batched requests. Rollup aggregates both. We should dedupe by request_id or prefer vector units for embeddings.
Sam (Eng): Quick remediation options: (A) UI-side prefer 'vectors' when both units present for a bucket (low-risk, fast), (B) adjust rollup job to dedupe on request_id (safer for billing but slower), (C) run a backfill to collapse duplicates and correct historical rollups. I'll prepare PRs for A+B and schedule C.
Maria (Support): Customer ok with UI band-aid as long as billing team investigates. Escalating to finance. @finance please advise on holding charges until we confirm.
Sam (Eng): Opening PR for UI guard: https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/9834 — filters out 'tokens' when 'vectors' > 0 for same interval. Deploying to canary.
Lee (Analytics): Starting backfill job to collapse duplicate metrics by request_id and unit priority. Backfill ETA ~6h, running on analytics-backfill-2. I'll post job id when started.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: console-canary - ref=pr/9834 - 5% traffic.
Sam (Eng): After canary validates, we'll ramp. For billing reconciliation we'll need list of affected customer_ids + amounts where rollup summed both units. Lee, can you export bd-4471 timeframe and run the double-count detection query?
Lee (Analytics): Exported file: s3://redwood-exports/dedupe/bd-4471-2026-03-10-11.csv. Also running clusterwide detection to get customer-level exposures.
Maria (Support): I'll share canary update with the customer: UI change in canary now, backfill in progress, billing investigation queued. They'll wait for billing reconciliation but want a clear timeline.
Sam (Eng): cc @oncall for billing reconciliation. Follow-up tasks: Rollup dedupe PR, backfill monitoring, finance reconciliation ticket.
Maria (Support): Thanks team. I'll keep customer updated and paste finance ticket here when created. :thumbsup:
Sam (Eng): Good catch. We'll prioritize the rollup fix for billing correctness even after UI patch.
Lee (Analytics): Noted. Will also add an assertion to the ingest test that prevents emitting both legacy token_count and new vector_count for the same request.
Maria (Support): Perfect. Closing loop: customer notified, temporary display fix rolled to canary, backfill + billing investigation running. Will reopen if anything changes.
